decisions.reason: Because A is close to the core postpress offer and was marketed on its own page, management would likely keep it while tolerating some early uncertainty unless orders clearly miss aspiration levels.

B is more distant from the established offer, so its performance hurdle is higher, but its flagship status and fit with the move toward digitally connected finishing make management likely to give it more time before reallocating resources.
C builds directly on existing systems and capabilities, so comparable-firm aspirations are easier to meet and the firm has little reason to drop it quickly.

D is both close to the established portfolio and publicly emphasized as a strategic focus, so boundedly rational management would be very likely to retain it unless results were clearly disappointing.
E fits the firm’s booklet-making and binding activities well, and the broad portfolio and service slack support keeping it while the market response becomes clearer.
F had lower website prominence, which suggests weaker early traction, but as a close add-on to the existing folding business it is still more likely to be retained than dropped in the near term.
